witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.label | test("-- trading/dealer_scenario_checkpoint_v1::")) | select((.label | test("checkpoint_commit_v1")) | not) | select(.wire_bytes != null) | .wire_bytes] | max | (. < 1232) | tostring
witnesses.provenance: Solana's PACKET_DATA_SIZE is 1,232 bytes. ProgramTest submits no packet and cannot enforce it -- Found31 is the defect class that produced -- so the campaign serialises each legacy transaction itself and compares the MEASURED extent. Six of the seven stages fit with room: cleanup 276, evaluate 409, create 541, page 871, reserve 1,026, rollback 1,026. Commit is excluded here because it genuinely does not fit, which the next witness pins rather than hides.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.label | test("checkpoint_commit_v1")) | select(.wire_bytes != null) | .wire_bytes] | max | (. > 1232) | tostring
witnesses.provenance: The one commit this campaign submits as a LEGACY transaction measures 1,366 bytes -- over Solana's 1,232-byte limit. That is exactly why every other commit travels as a v0 transaction over an Address Lookup Table. Asserted positively so the fact cannot quietly stop being true: if commit ever shrinks below the limit, someone should decide deliberately whether the lookup table is still wanted, rather than discovering it from a green run.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.wire_bytes == null) | select(.label | test(" -- trading/")) | select((.label | test("checkpoint_commit_v1")) | not)] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: A null wire_bytes says the campaign did not measure, which is honest and is NOT a claim that the frame fits -- and the packet witnesses above take a max that would silently drop those rows. This pins that the unmeasured checkpoint rows are all commit rows, the ones that travel v0 over a lookup table. If a future stage started travelling v0 without saying so, this stops being zero.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select((.label | test("-- trading/")) | not) | select(.wire_bytes != null and .wire_bytes >= 1232)] | length | (. > 0) | tostring
witnesses.provenance: The Hot execution rows in this campaign measure 2,342 to 3,084 bytes: they do NOT fit a Solana packet and could not be submitted to a cluster as they stand. That is a finding, not an accident, and it is the reason those rows are bound with no route claim -- recording them as evidence for a route would credit a route on a frame no validator would accept. This witness asserts the fact positively so that it cannot quietly stop being true without someone noticing.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.label | test(" -- trading/")) | select((.label | test(" -- trading/dealer_scenario_checkpoint_v1::process_dealer_scenario_checkpoint_(create|page|evaluate|reserve|rollback|commit|cleanup)_v1 -- ")) | not)] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: The label's route half is read off the submitted bytes with the program's OWN dispatch predicates (`is_dealer_scenario_checkpoint_*_v1`), so a label cannot name a route Trading would not take. This pins that nothing else ever appears in that position -- a hand-edited label, or a predicate set that drifted from the dispatcher, fails here rather than quietly binding a route to the wrong evidence.

The emitter refuses an empty label, so this should be structurally impossible. It is here because the census's dedup and binding both key on the label, and a campaign that ever produced one would bind coverage to nothing.
